Read and write the cells of an Excel workbook

Source: R/sp_workbook.R
sp_workbook.Rd

These functions use the Excel REST API to work with a workbook stored in SharePoint or OneDrive without downloading and uploading the whole file. Changes are made to the live workbook so edits by other people are not overwritten. The workbook must be an .xlsx file.

  • sp_workbook_sheets() lists the worksheets in a workbook.

  • sp_workbook_range_read() reads a range (or the used range) of a worksheet into a data frame.

  • sp_workbook_range_write() writes a data frame, matrix, or vector to a range.

Use local_sp_workbook_session() to make several requests in one workbook session, or sp_workbook_session_create() and sp_workbook_session_close() to manage the session yourself.

Usage

sp_workbook_sheets(x, ..., session_id = NULL, call = caller_env())

sp_workbook_range_read(
  x,
  range = NULL,
  ...,
  sheet = NULL,
  header = TRUE,
  session_id = NULL,
  call = caller_env()
)

sp_workbook_range_write(
  x,
  values,
  range = "A1",
  ...,
  sheet = NULL,
  col_names = TRUE,
  session_id = NULL,
  call = caller_env()
)

Arguments

x

A SharePoint or OneDrive Excel workbook. Can be a ms_drive_item object, a SharePoint URL, or a path passed to get_sp_item().

...

Additional parameters passed to get_sp_item() if x is not a ms_drive_item object.

session_id

A workbook session ID from sp_workbook_session_create(). If NULL (default), the session for the workbook set by local_sp_workbook_session() or the sharepointr.workbook_session option is used, if any. Otherwise the request is sent without a session.

call

The execution environment used in error messages. Defaults to the environment of the calling function.

range

A range in A1 notation (e.g. "A1:C3"). If NULL, sp_workbook_range_read() reads the used range of the worksheet. For sp_workbook_range_write(), range can be a single cell, which is expanded to fit values.

sheet

Worksheet name or ID. If NULL, the first worksheet is used. A sheet name can also be included in range (e.g. "Sheet1!A1:C3").

header

If TRUE (default), the first row of the range is used for column names.

values

A data frame, matrix, or vector. A vector is written as a single column. NA values are written as empty cells.

col_names

If TRUE (default), the column names of a data frame (or matrix with column names) are written as the first row.

Value

  • sp_workbook_sheets(): A data frame with a row for each worksheet.

  • sp_workbook_range_read(): A data frame.

  • sp_workbook_range_write(): The address of the range written to, invisibly.

Reading after writing

Requests sent without a session may not see each other's changes right away. Writes are saved to the workbook, but a read sent without a session straight afterward can return the earlier values for a short time. To read back what you wrote, make the write and the read in the same session (e.g. with local_sp_workbook_session()). Requests in a session see the changes made in that session immediately.

See also

Other workbooks: local_sp_workbook_session(), sp_workbook_session_create()

Examples

sp_workbook_url <- "<SharePoint workbook url>"

if (is_sp_url(sp_workbook_url)) {
  sp_workbook_sheets(sp_workbook_url)

  sp_workbook_range_read(sp_workbook_url, "A1:C10")
}
